definition: Desertion is the act of leaving or abandoning the side, group, or cause to which one had belonged. In the historical passage here, it refers to a prominent member quitting one faction and thereby strengthening its opponents.

provenance.revision: 1901 New York Macmillan original; archive index checked 2026-10-18
provenance.scope: Source record Mohammedanism; pinned source text

reasons: The packet does not provide a general definition of “desertion” as “the act of leaving or abandoning the side, group, or cause to which one had belonged.” It only mentions “the desertion from their ranks of the celebrated Hasan al-Ash'arí.”

The second sentence’s specifics are only partially supported: the packet supports that Hasan al-Ash'arí “desertion from their ranks” benefited “their adversaries” by providing “controversial weapons,” but the packet does not explicitly describe this as “thereby strengthening its opponents” in those exact terms, nor does it frame desertion as “quitting one faction” in a generalized way.
